headline: Exporting the same three modules as JSX components instead of style values costs every lane, hand-written vanilla included, and costs next-yak its fold outright: a styled component cannot be folded across a module boundary.

microbench.why: The declarations, the three modules and the rendered element are identical to the Example `button-variants` shown above; only the API changes. Every lane pays for that. `vanilla` falls from 1.79M to 1.39M renders/s purely for the two extra React components in the tree, which prices an unfoldable component API before any library is involved. `next-yak` falls further, from 2.12M to 1.19M, because `styled(Button)` declared in another module leaves `fold_jsx_usages` nothing to rewrite, and it ends up indistinguishable from its own `foldStatic: false` lane, whose spread overlaps it in both runs. The atomic lanes give up least, `stylex` from 1.35M to 1.05M, since they were already merging at render.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` at 1,143 req/s, `vanilla` at 1,125 and `next-yak-nofold` at 1,113 finish within 3% of each other, which is the shape of a case where nobody folds. `styled-components` at 685 req/s fares relatively better here than on the value form, since a component API is the shape it was designed around.

attribution.why: `vanilla` posts the lowest total at 0.750 ms, with 0.309 ms of component self-time for the three nested functions and no library at all. `next-yak` needs 0.940 ms, 0.409 ms of it lib self-time inside the `Yak` wrappers folding would have removed, and `next-yak-nofold` records 0.369 ms in that same slice, which confirms nothing folded. `emotion` at 2.93 ms and `goober` at 1.86 ms stay dominated by their serializers.

hydrate.why: The compile-time lanes group between 46.0 ms and 49.6 ms while the sheet-building lanes trail at 139 ms for `goober` and 115 ms for `emotion`. Component depth costs almost nothing on this axis, because hydration matches markup that already exists rather than creating it.

inp.why: Eleven lanes answer a single click between 6.5 ms and 7.8 ms, indistinguishable at this spread. Only `goober` at 11.0 ms and `emotion` at 10.2 ms separate from the group.

mount.why: Cold mount compresses twelve lanes into 71.5 ms through 86.9 ms, with `next-yak-nofold` at 71.5 ms and `next-yak` at 73.0 ms tied inside their spreads. Extra fibers cost render time, and layout is what dominates a mount.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, costing 0.129 ms to 0.183 ms. The API shape changes what React does, not what the style engine has to match.

payload.why: `vanilla` ships 3,164 gz B with no JS. `next-yak` ships 4,078 B, which is 189 B more than the same ladder written as style values, because the component form keeps three wrappers instead of one folded class. The runtime libraries are unchanged from the value form, 13.5 kB of JS for `styled-components` and 13.0 kB for `emotion`, since what they ship is the library rather than the ladder.

nsweep.why: `next-yak` at 2.88 ms and `next-yak-nofold` at 2.93 ms trace the same line, which states the case as plainly as it can be stated: folding that cannot cross a module boundary is worth nothing at any size. `vanilla` at 3.10 ms sits just behind them, `emotion` at 10.6 ms sets the far end.

crossCase: This is the Example `button-variants` shown above with each module exporting a JSX component instead of a style value, so the pair prices the API shape rather than the file layout — both are split three ways. The same asymmetry runs through the Example `multifile-shop`: exported values fold across a boundary, exported components do not. The css-prop lanes have no cell here at all, because the css prop cannot take a style fragment as a component prop and the case does not compile for them, which is a limitation worth knowing before choosing that API.
